targets.title: Erdos Problem #413 — barriers for omega
targets.prompt: Erdős problem #413. Let omega(m) be the number of distinct prime divisors of m. Call n a barrier when m + omega(m) <= n for every natural number m < n. Determine whether there are infinitely many such n. A relaxed open variant asks whether there exists epsilon > 0 for which infinitely many n satisfy m + epsilon*omega(m) <= n for every m < n. Retrieve the exact current primary statement and status before working. Seek a complete proof only if every original quantifier closes; otherwise provide rigorous reusable partial progress, exact equivalent reformulations, verified computations with reproducible certificates, and the precise endpoint obstruction. Distinguish omega from Omega and do not present the relaxed variant or finite computation as a solution. Source identifiers: https://www.erdosproblems.com/413, FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/413.lean, and OEIS A005236.
